articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue
articles.content_orig:
A missile industry veteran has been tapped as Iran's new defense minister, replacing the previous minister who was killed on Feb. 28, the first day of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran.
Iranian parliamentarians overwhelmingly approved the appointment of Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, 68, as the country's new defense chief on Sunday.
Akhlaghi studied chemical engineering at Amirkabir University of Technology and then spent more than four decades working in Iran's military industries, holding senior positions in the Shahid Bagheri Industrial Group, the Aerospace Industries Organization  – which has worked on missile development in cooperation with Russia, China and North Korea –  and the Defense Industries Organization.
He worked with Hassan Tehrani Moghaddam, a senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander widely regarded as the father of Iran's missile industry.
Akhlaghi has been under international sanctions since 2007 because of his involvement in Iran's missile programs.
His appointment comes as Iran works to rebuild its military facilities and replenish weapons lost during the war. He has pledged to strengthen domestic arms production, and his background suggests rebuilding Iran's missile programs will be a priority for the ministry.
Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia has claimed repeatedly since late August that Iran has rebuilt its weapons manufacturing capacity, including last week, when it said the country was now able to make more arms than " even before it [the war] began ."
Early in the war, the U.S. military said it had destroyed more than 85% of Iran's "defense industrial base," and President Trump had previously claimed Iran's military capabilities were destroyed by U.S. strikes, but experts have questioned that assessment, and Iran has demonstrated an ongoing capacity to launch attacks on ships in the region.
A Qatari aircraft arrived in Tehran Tuesday just minutes after a plane carrying Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, departed. The Qatari plane left the Iranian capital approximately 30 minutes later, according to aviation tracking data cited by Iran's semi-official Fars News agency.
The aircraft's short stay raised questions about whether it might have been carrying a diplomatic message amid ongoing indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran. Qatar is among the nations that have acted as mediators between the two sides for months.
No information about the aircraft's passengers or why it was in Tehran for only half an hour were provided in the Fars report.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they had targeted a Saudi military operations room at Badr Camp in Aden, in southwest Yemen, with a ballistic missile on Wednesday.
Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, in a post on X , called the strike a direct hit.
"Our armed forces successfully targeted the enemy Saudi operations room at Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile. The strike was accurate and direct," he said.
Aden is the de facto seat of power of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, which was forced to decamp after the Houthis occupied the national capital Sanaa more than a decade ago.
The attack claimed by the Houthis Wednesday was the third in a week on Aden.
A police official in Aden told the French news agency AFP earlier that there had been a blast "caused by a Houthi missile." Two other security sources told AFP the strike targeted a site near the city's airport.
A senior official from Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure comes under attack.
Brig. Gen. Yadollah Javani, the IRGC's deputy for political affairs, warned Iran would use its full capabilities to retaliate if the U.S. and its allies launch new attacks against Iranian infrastructure. He said various investments and assets, including undersea cables carrying internet data in the strategic waterway, could be among the targets of Iranian retaliation if hostilities resume.
"The Americans and their allies have significant investments, and if they want to damage our infrastructure, it is natural that the Islamic Republic will use all its capabilities and easily destroy their investments and assets, including the internet cables that pass beneath the waters of the Strait of Hormuz," he said.
Analysts say cutting the cables in the waterway would most likely affect internet connectivity in Persian Gulf countries .
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Tehran and Washington were still engaged in indirect negotiations via mediators over the seven-day ceasefire proposal presented by Iran in September.
Araghchi said the U.S. was seeking to add further clauses to the Iranian proposal, which Mr. Trump rejected last month.
The proposal called for the end of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil sales, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
He said Pakistan and Qatar were among the nations facilitating the indirect talks between Iran and the U.S., as they have been for months.
"The negotiating table remains in place," Araghchi said. "It is the American side that is closing the path, not Iran."
U.S. diplomatic missions across the Middle East have issued a new round of security warnings to Americans amid escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia, including an Oct. 10 strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed an American citizen.
The alerts, issued Sunday by U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries, warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting. The advisories urged Americans to exercise vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.
"We are actively warning U.S. citizens about the very real threat the Houthis pose and urging them to heed official guidance," Edgar Vasquez, the State Department's deputy assistant secretary for press, told CBS News.
"These alerts are part of a proactive effort by the Trump administration to ensure Americans are aware of potential risks," Vasquez said, adding that the safety and security of American citizens remain the department's "top priority."
President Trump said the U.S. is "doing very well with Iran" and he's just deciding how he wants to win the war.
"As you know, we're doing very well with Iran," Mr. Trump said as he took questions from reporters in the Oval Office at an unrelated executive order signing. "We just have to make a final decision of which way do we want to win? Do we want to win the nice way or the not nice way? But we're doing very well."
The war, which Mr. Trump said would take only a few weeks in March, has now dragged on for almost eight months with no apparent end in sight. Iran said on Tuesday it would not return to the negotiating table unless the U.S. drops its sanctions, threats and pressure campaign — an unlikely demand.
The president also discussed Europe not helping the U.S. with the war with Iran, saying, "We don't need any help. But I was testing them."
"I just called individual presidents and prime ministers to ask, would they like to help us? And they said, 'No,'" Mr. Trump said. "I said, 'Well, that's not nice.' You know, we spend hundreds of billions a year on NATO. And they said no."

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Opens Higher; SpaceX Shares Surge on Tesla Deal Talks — Live Updates
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Opens Higher; SpaceX Shares Surge on Tesla Deal Talks — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX stock jumped Wednesday after the company reported surging revenue growth in its third quarter, and owner Elon Musk floated a potential SpaceX- Tesla merger.
The space company, which made its debut on the Nasdaq in the biggest initial public offering ever in June, reported third-quarter revenue on Tuesday of $14.6 billion, up 161% from the previous year, and beating LSEG consensus estimates of $12.72 billion.
Meanwhile, its operating income came in at $2.8 billion, with net income of $4.4 billion, after reporting a net loss of $1.05 billion in the same period a year earlier.
On an earnings call, Musk said he's considering a combination with Tesla — which would mark the largest merger in history — and that the boards of both companies have created specific committees to discuss a consolidation.
"I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating," Musk said on the call. Tesla is set to report third-quarter earnings after the closing bell on Wednesday.
Shares of other space stocks, including Rocket Lab , Intuitive Machines and AST SpaceMobile climbed on Wednesday.
SpaceX forecasts first-quarter 2027 revenue between $33 billion and $37 billion, beating the average analyst estimate of $22.2 billion, according to LSEG.
"We delivered another strong quarter in Q3. Revenue grew an impressive 161% year-over-year, fueled by continued momentum in Connectivity and a clear inflection in our Super Intelligence business," SpaceX's chief financial officer, Bret Johnsen, said in the earnings release.
Johnsen pinned the strong results on recurring revenue from its satellite internet business, Starlink , and significant expansion of its Super Intelligence [SI] infrastructure.
The company has dived into artificial intelligence this year, which it's now calling SI. The segment is its largest business unit, with revenue soaring ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year.
Commentary on computing during the earnings call supported "continued pricing power and shorter payback periods" for AI cloud providers, Truist Securities analysts said in a Tuesday note.
"Despite market concerns relating to financing for AI cloud providers this past week, we believe SpaceX's third-quarter 2026 represents the first data point during the earnings season to support the bull case for AI cloud providers," they added.
They explained that demand appears "insatiable," with SpaceX noting that it could rent out its capacity several times over. The analysts said Coreweave and Nebius are set to benefit and capture demand as "pricing power will more than offset higher rates."
The shares of neoclouds Nebius and Coreweave traded marginally lower, while Iren and Applied Digital climbed in early trading on Wednesday.
— CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: Intel Stock Is Under Pressure After Musk Signals Terafab Breakthrough
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk initially tried to buy manufacturing facilities from Intel, TSMC and Micron before embarking on his ambitious Terafab project, says a fresh report from the Korean media. The report, courtesy of The Elec, covers the different suppliers Terafab has been working with and adds that the speed of execution at the project has left many suppliers surprised. Through Terafab, industry observers expect an initial production of 100,000 wafers per month before 2030 before scaling up to Musk's ambitious goal of a million wafers a month.
Musk's Terafab, through which he aims to produce a whopping 1 million wafers per month eventually, is a source of considerable debate. Earlier this month, reports surfaced that the executive was in talks with Taiwan's TSMC for a partnership. Soon afterward, Musk clarified that the maximum role that TSMC could play in the project would be that of a subcontractor.
Similarly, TSMC's CEO, Dr. C.C. Wei, remarked during the firm's latest earnings call that his firm was in discussions with Musk but asserted that it must run the plants in order for a partnership to work.
While Musk has grand plans for the chip facility, with the initial output of Terafab expected to be 100,000 wafers per month, it would barely make a dent in the global chip manufacturing industry. Compared to TSMC, the Taiwanese chip giant in particular is expected to manufacture 120,000 wafers of its leading-edge 2-nanometer manufacturing technology by 2026 end.
Now, a report from The Elec claims that Terafab has already entered into discussions with Korean suppliers. The list of companies also includes American firms Lam Research and Applied Materials, and overall Terafab is working with firms that provide piping, polishing slurries, cleaning chemicals and other materials involved in the semiconductor supply chain .
Crucially, the report also adds that building Terafab from the ground up was not Musk's initial plan. Instead, the SpaceX and Tesla CEO had first considered buying facilities from Micron, intel and TSMC. However, after he was "turned down" he shifted toward partnerships. Intel has directly partnered with Terafab and will work with the Musk project through its 14A manufacturing technology.
Terafab is part of Musk's plan to build enough chips for his autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots and other endeavors. These projects, in turn, factor into the executive's plans of expanding the economy beyond Earth.
In a podcast with Walter Isaacson recorded in August, the executive explained his plans. Responding to a question about whether physical AI would be more valuable than virtual AI, Musk remarks that "the value of intelligence becomes exponentially greater. Because it can now do things. It can have a science lab and run experiments."
In economic terms, Musk believes that "digital super intelligence probably improves the output of goods and services by 20 to 30%, something like that. So call it like maybe a 30% increase in the economy of Earth. It's still significant. It's like $30 trillion dollars a year, incremental."
However, with robots that allow you to "get to space" and "do a mass driver on the Moon, then you can get to, I think potentially, a million times of the size of the Earth economy," he said.

articles.title_orig: Shader Compilation Stutter Begone: Nvidia's Latest GPU Drivers Finally Add Advanced Shader Delivery
articles.title_zh: Shader Compilation Stutter Begone: Nvidia's Latest GPU Drivers Finally Add Advanced Shader Delivery
articles.content_orig:
At the start of October, Nvidia announced that it would soon be adding Microsoft's Advanced Shader Delivery (ASD) technology to its RTX and RTX Spark graphics drivers in the continuing fight against the shader compilation stutter that has become increasingly commonplace in modern PC gaming. With version 621.01 , released today, ASD support is now finally in place.
ASD is designed to prevent the momentary hitches experienced in games when a shader needs to be compiled on the fly, often when a new model or effect appears for the first time. Most modern games include a shader burn when you first launch a game (or update your graphics drivers), but it's still common for some shaders to be missed by this step. ASD works by downloading precompiled shaders from the cloud for your specific graphics hardware on Windows 11. It's a similar approach to the Linux-based Steam Shader Pre-Caching system established by Valve for the Steam Deck.
This normally "just works", with no user involvement, though developers need to specifically support the technology. If you want to test it out, two high-profile releases with support are Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
As well as eliminating troublesome shader compilation stutter, the technology also massively speeds up that initial precompilation step - Microsoft says it is reduced by up to 95 percent . Given that this can take upwards of 20 minutes even on high-end systems in some games, that's a meaningful improvement.
However, this technology doesn't help prevent traversal stutter, another hitch-causing phenomenon related to data being loaded into and out of memory when passing an invisible boundary in the game world.
Nvidia also has a technology to prevent shaders from being wiped out following a graphics driver update called Automatic Shader Compilation , and the two technologies can be used in concert.
To benefit from Advanced Shader Delivery support, you'll need to be using Windows 11 24H2 or later and update to Nvidia's 621.01 driver via the Nvidia app or by manually downloading the installer - I had to opt for the latter as the driver wasn't showing as available in the app for my PC.
Note that ASD is already part of AMD and Qualcomm's graphics driver and is also set to arrive for Intel discrete and integrated graphics later this month, though an official release date or graphics driver version number has not yet been set.

articles.title_zh: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is set to publicly file its S-1 investor prospectus as soon as Friday, according to three people familiar with the artificial intelligence firm's plans. The move would mark a crucial next step for what could be the biggest IPO in history.
The much-anticipated public debut , expected to surpass SpaceX's ( SPCX ) June IPO, is widely viewed as a crucial test of investor appetite for the artificial intelligence boom, as investors have become more concerned about the industry's massive spending.
Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft IPO registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in June. Under SEC rules, companies using the confidential process must make their registration materials available 15 calendar days before the start of their formal investor roadshow.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment on the timing of its S-1.
A public filing would clear a key procedural hurdle toward a potential November listing, though the timing of the offering remains subject to market conditions and other factors. Crucially, it would also give regular investors their first look at the financial details and risks around one of the AI industry's fastest-growing companies.
Anthropic is spending billions on AI infrastructure to train and run its suite of Claude models. That includes working with Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), as well as renting out graphics processor unit (GPU) capacity from SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center.
The company pulled in $16.3 billion in revenue over the first six months of 2026 and reported a net loss of over $80 billion, according to a Tuesday Wall Street Journal report . Wall Street is anticipating that the company could raise as much as $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters previously reported .
Last week, Anthropic told investors at its San Francisco office that its revenue climbed to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up from $11.5 billion in the second quarter, according to the Financial Times , noting that the company is also profitable on an adjusted basis.
The colossal offering comes as this year's banner IPO market is becoming more challenging. Earlier this week, shares of South Korean data center provider Elice plummeted a staggering 32% during its first trading day after raising $151 million. Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid abruptly shelved plans for a public listing earlier this month after investors balked at its proposed valuation, while several other companies have postponed plans to go public, citing market conditions.
Publicly traded AI-related companies have also waffled in recent days as investors become more selective over the industry's enormous spending needs. CoreWeave, in particular, has come under sharp scrutiny as investors question its future revenue prospects relative to its debt load.
The shift highlights how investors who enthusiastically bid up AI-related companies earlier this year have become more selective.
Given its enormous size, the timing of Anthropic's IPO is also expected to be a significant factor for other companies seeking to go public in the coming weeks, one person said.
CEO Dario Amodei co-founded Anthropic with his sister Daniela, the company's president.
Anthropic established a strong foothold in the enterprise market with its Claude chatbot, the popular AI coding tool Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.
Rival OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), which was initially expected to launch its IPO this year, is now projected to hit the public markets in early 2027.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.content_orig:
The logo of Tesla is displayed on a smartphone screen with the SpaceX logo in the background.
The world’s richest man has publicly backed a potential combination of SpaceX and Tesla in what could be the biggest merger in history.
On Tuesday, Elon Musk , the CEO and largest shareholder of both companies, said the electric vehicle maker and the rocket company had formed special committees at the request of shareholders to discuss the idea.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, ​and there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating,” Musk told SpaceX investors on a conference call.
“I think it would be a good ​idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies,” he added.
The committees, which are made up of independent directors, would need to agree on the transaction terms of any deal before putting it to shareholders for a vote. Musk said his conflict of interest prevents him from participating in their discussions.
Musk has previously teased a Tesla-SpaceX merger. On a July 22 earnings call, Musk said there was “more and more overlap” between Tesla and SpaceX as the companies expand into artificial intelligence and robotics. Last week, Barclays analysts suggested that a merger could be announced before Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting in December.
Tuesday’s call was the first confirmation that the companies were formally exploring a combination.
A merger could create a company worth around $3.5 trillion , putting it among the world’s most valuable companies. It could also become the biggest merger ever by deal value, potentially surpassing SpaceX’s record-setting $250 billion acquisition of Musk-owned AI company xAI in February. SpaceX is currently valued at about $2 trillion, and Tesla at $1.5 trillion. A deal could also help propel Musk back into trillionaire ranks , depending on its terms and how investors value the combined company. Musk owns around 48% of SpaceX and 20% of Tesla.
The shares of both companies rose in after-hours trading on Tuesday. SpaceX, which went public in June, reported a quarterly net profit of $4.4 billion. Musk told investors he expects annual recurring revenue of between $500 billion and $1 trillion by the end of 2027.
Some analysts, however, have warned of regulatory and geopolitical hurdles, particularly in terms of Tesla’s Chinese operations and SpaceX’s U.S. defence work. Morningstar analysts said a merger could raise U.S. national security concerns involving the combined company’s supply chain. JPMorgan analysts also flagged regulatory approval in China as a potential stumbling block.
Any deal could also face congressional scrutiny, which could intensify if Democrats win control of either chamber in the coming midterm elections. Democratic lawmakers have previously questioned Musk over conflicts of interest and raised national security concerns about reported Chinese investments in SpaceX. Democrats have also challenged major acquisitions in the past on consumer protection grounds. In June, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D, Mass.) criticized SpaceX’s IPO, citing Musk’s concentrated voting power and weak investor protections—concerns that could resurface in a Tesla-SpaceX merger.
A merger could bring two of Musk’s biggest businesses under one corporate umbrella, making it easier for the companies to move investments and resources between projects. “This would allow him to run all their operations under one roof without tripping on as many governance issues,” wrote Morningstar analysts Seth Goldstein and Nicolas Owens in June. “For example, Musk could move Tesla software developers or engineers to work on SpaceX AI projects, and vice versa, or have Tesla and SpaceX supply one another without the need for related party transaction disclosures or risking shareholder lawsuits claiming the resources of one firm are being diverted for the benefit of the other.”
Analysts noted that Tesla’s robotaxis could benefit from Starlink connectivity, while its autonomous vehicles and Optimus humanoid robots could more closely integrate SpaceX’s AI technology. SpaceX’s planned orbital data centers, meanwhile, could potentially benefit from access to Tesla’s battery and energy storage products.
A combined company could also mean greater control of several stages of the AI value chain, from chip design and planned manufacturing to computing infrastructure, AI software, and its deployment in vehicles and robots.
The companies already collaborate. In March, they announced Terafab , a joint semiconductor manufacturing project intended to produce chips for Tesla’s vehicles and humanoid robots and SpaceX’s planned AI satellites. SpaceX technologies have also been used in some Tesla products, including the new Roadster prototype , which uses SpaceX-developed thrusters.
David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group, told the BBC that a merger also appears to align with Musk’s long-held ambition of colonizing Mars . Musk previously outlined plans to send Tesla’s Optimus robots to the planet aboard SpaceX’s Starship spacecraft.
A merger could also strengthen Musk’s influence over Tesla’s direction. Barclays estimated that a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla could give Musk around 37% of the combined company while controlling around 56% of its voting power. He currently controls around 82% of voting power at SpaceX and 20% at Tesla . That could represent either a benefit or a risk for shareholders, as decision-making would become faster but have fewer checks.
“One thing I don’t think people talk enough about with SpaceX and Tesla as well: You do still have a huge amount of key-man risk here,” wrote Morningstar analyst David Sekera earlier this month. “God forbid anything were to happen to Elon Musk.”

articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: Critical PHP vulnerabilities patched, update now!
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: Critical PHP vulnerabilities patched, update now!
articles.content_orig:
The PHP development team has released emergency security updates to fix PHP2Shell, two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that could let attackers execute code remotely on web servers without logging in. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately.
“These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability  required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit,” Wiz researchers explained .
Every PHP installation that serves web requests is affected, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Setups using mod_php face the greatest danger. A working exploit has already shown that a single unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.
“The PHP situation will lead to a mass of incidents – it’s one of the biggest vulns in years,” noted security researcher Kevin Beaumont.
CVE-2026-109618 – RCE via OOM corruption : out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.
CVE-2026-109619 – RCE via stale global state : request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.
The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to consider taking offline any system that can’t be fixed right away.
“So many embedded installations out there that will never be patched. Too many forgotten, unmaintained apps. There will be a long tail for this one,” commented computer forensics expert Hal Pomeranz.
Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Downloads are available here .
Linux distributions and long-term support (LTS) vendors got the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check with their vendor for updated packages.
The PHP project no longer supports PHP 8.1 and earlier versions. Some distributions and LTS vendors offer backported fixes, so users on these versions should contact their vendor or upgrade to a supported release.
Anyone who relies on rpms.remirepo.net , a volunteer-maintained repository, is advised to switch to distribution packages or build PHP from source so they can patch immediately. The repository will not have updates available today.
Because the vulnerabilities are so severe, the PHP security team has also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. These are meant for people who build from source or who don’t have an LTS vendor.
“PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free,” said Dane Knecht, CTO at Cloudflare.

articles.title_zh: How We Draw Lines in a World Awash in A.I. Images
articles.content_orig:
When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn't affect our editorial independence .
I remember when AI images were easy to spot thanks to dead giveaways like freakishly mutated hands, warped faces, and Escher-like architecture. That was way back in 2023. Since then, things have progressed fast. AI image generators now are so good that it’s genuinely hard to tell what’s real and what isn’t.
But that doesn’t stop us humans from thinking we still have an eye for what’s real and what’s fake. So if you still think you’ve got it, then go ahead and give it a try with Slop Sense . It’s a free website with a handful of games that put your AI-detecting skills to the test.
My favorite game is called Reality Check where you’re shown an image and have to guess whether it’s a real photo or an AI-generated one. You get 10 seconds to make each guess and 60 seconds to rack up as many points as possible.
You’ll earn points for correct guesses, lose points for mistakes, and get bonuses for stringing together correct answers. When the timer runs out, you can go back through the images and see which ones tripped you up. It even provides the prompt used to generate the AI images. My score was shockingly abysmal at 12 out of 22 correct.
There’s also Ghostwriter, which takes the same idea but asks you to guess which text is written by AI and which is written by humans. I actually found this to be easier, but that may be because my job involves actually writing text all day.
These are a fun time waster and if nothing else, they’re an eye opening experience for how convincing AI-generated images and text are becoming—think about that the next time you’re mindlessly scrolling through social media confidently thinking you know what’s AI slop and what’s not.
Oh, and the irony of using AI to build games about spotting AI isn’t lost on me.

It's an important development for the Xbox platform, given that Sony has already released two versions of its PSSR machine learning upscaler for PS5 Pro and recently backported a lightweight version called QSSR to the base PS5 . Now, Microsoft's ML hardware on the Xbox Series X and Series S might finally come in useful - despite launching with the consoles in 2020, we've not seen it used for upscaling thus far.

Either way, FSR 4.1 is capable of producing better results than the older FSR 3 model, and it'll be fascinating to see how it compares to the likes of FSR, Epic's TSR, and Sony's QSSR and PSSR in shipping games.
Microsoft has also worked with Asus and AMD to add FSR 4.1 support to Xbox Ally and Xbox Ally X handhelds, which is now available. I'm working on a review of the Intel-powered Acer Predator Atlas 8 handheld right now, and it'll be interesting to compare how the Xbox Ally X with FSR 4.1 and Atlas 8 with XeSS 3 compare in terms of image quality and performance.

Boeing's largest 737 MAX aircraft has received Federal Aviation Administration certification, clearing the way for deliveries of a jet with 1,555 orders that represent a third of the company's outstanding 737 MAX order book.
The FAA announced Tuesday that it had certified the 737 MAX 10 after years of regulatory and safety reviews, removing a major hurdle for Boeing as it prepares to begin deliveries to airlines in the coming months.
Boeing said the aircraft has received orders from more than 30 customers worldwide, making the MAX 10 a key part of the company's commercial airplane backlog.
The approval also marks a significant milestone for Boeing's 737 MAX program, which has received 7,350 orders across the aircraft family, with nearly 2,500 planes delivered through the end of September 2026.

Certification followed an extensive FAA safety review and testing program. Boeing said the process involved nearly 1,000 test flights, more than 2,000 flight hours and 1,000 hours of ground testing.

"This is a major win for American manufacturing and our nation's status as a global aviation powerhouse," Duffy said in the FAA's announcement.

Robust crude oil flows out of the Middle East in recent weeks have started to pressure the key metric of strength for physical supply out of the region.
The premium of Oman crude over Dubai, the measure of Middle East’s market strength, has slumped this week to the lowest level since the end of July, to $4.22 per barrel, according to data by General Index cited by Bloomberg .
The Oman-Dubai crude differential had soared to as high as $65 in March when the Strait of Hormuz was at a virtual closure and no crude cargoes were moving out of the Middle East. The premium of Oman crude later slipped into a discount in the three weeks in the middle of June and early July, during which the U.S. and Iran were looking to negotiate a deal.
The differential blew out again in August and especially in September, when hostilities resumed.
But as the Middle Eastern producers accelerated shuttle-shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, flows have recovered in recent weeks.
The higher availability, especially of spot cargoes, led to the Oman crude premium to Dubai slumping from as high as $30 per barrel in the middle of September to just above $4 per barrel this week, per data by General Index.
Crude oil flows from the Middle East are recovering; many tanker-tracking services say they are even topping pre-war levels.
But the cost to move the crude out of the region is very high—freight rates have soared to record highs amid a shortage of tankers. The increased oil flows from the Strait of Hormuz, mostly thanks to ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Gulf of Oman, are tying up supertankers for weeks waiting for the transfers outside the Strait, limiting the availability of very large crude carriers (VLCCs) for other key global oil trade routes, such as the U.S. Gulf Coast to Asia.

OpenAI will make its artificial intelligence models available for developers through Google's cloud, following years of competition between the two companies.
For OpenAI, the effort reflects a growing push to expand distribution of its technology to enterprise developers. That's critical as the ChatGPT creator looks to build its business beyond its consumer roots, and the move puts OpenAI's models on all three of the top cloud infrastructure providers.
Less than six months ago, OpenAI said Microsoft would no longer have the exclusive license on its intellectual property. The day after that ended, cloud leader Amazon unveiled plans to host OpenAI models .
Now Google is getting its shot, bringing OpenAI's GPT products to its cloud's model garden and Antigravity coding tool in the coming weeks.
"Google Cloud's longstanding investment in machine learning and AI has made it a destination for AI workloads and the developers and data scientists building them," OpenAI said in a blog post.
Google has been on a run in cloud computing this year. Annualized revenue growth in the segment accelerated to about 82% in the second quarter from 63% in the first quarter, thanks partly to strong demand for AI models and custom chips. Amazon and Microsoft posted second-quarter cloud growth of 37% and 42% , respectively. All three report quarterly results next week.
Most business spending on AI is on OpenAI and Anthropic, according to data from corporate card issuer Ramp, though some corporate IT departments have integrated Google's Gemini models into their systems. In September, Google announced its next-generation Gemini 4 Argon model.
OpenAI was founded in 2015 partly as a counterweight to the concentration of AI research at companies like Google. Two years later, Google employees submitted the influential Transformer academic paper that propelled AI, but it was OpenAI that helped bring the technology forward with ChatGPT. Now OpenAI is courting investors at a $1.4 trillion valuation and targeting an initial public offering.
Google and OpenAI previously partnered last year, when the AI lab said it was using Google's cloud to run ChatGPT and its application programming interface.

articles.title_orig: France's Macron vows order, calls foreign criticism of unrest 'stupid'
articles.title_zh: France's Macron vows order, calls foreign criticism of unrest 'stupid'
articles.content_orig:
Nationalist leaders are framing unrest as consequence of failed liberal governance and open borders
Europe’s far-right leaders have jumped on the violence that rocked numerous cities last weekend, framing it as the inevitable consequence of failed liberal governance and open-border policies and insisting only they can restore law and order.
Months away from key elections in Spain, France and Italy, authoritarian nationalists are eager to weaponise the wave of street unrest, originating in peaceful protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services but hijacked by violent rioters.
Those in opposition have not held back. In France, where cities such as Paris, Marseille and Lyon faced widespread rioting and looting, the far-right National Rally (RN) has denounced centrist incompetence and promised a crackdown.
The party’s president, Jordan Bardella, said the government was “impotent”. The RN leader, Marine Le Pen , said on Wednesday the state was “collapsing” and had “lost control of everything” amid “migratory, budgetary and security chaos”.
Ahead in presidential polls and seeking voters beyond her base, Le Pen has resisted explicitly racialising the unrest, but has framed it more broadly as a result of state and policy failures leading to “anarchic immigration” and “a total loss of authority”.
In Germany – where there were no major protests – the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) has stoked fears rioting could spill over the border. Its co-leader Alice Weidel said France’s “violent excesses” were a “warning for Germany”.
Weidel also linked the unrest to immigration, posting: “The dangerous mix of mass migration and leftwing extremism threatens to lead to civil war-like conditions here too … There will only be a turnaround on migration with the AfD!”
In Portugal , populists have used peaceful housing and cost of living protests to warn against “importing” instability. André Ventura of the far-right Chega party said the nation must “refrain from importing into Portugal climates of instability and protest”.
In Spain, where the housing crisis has led to huge protests and a Madrid encampment, and prompted the socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, to call a snap election next month, the far-right Vox party has sought to demonise the protesters. “They’re not defending the right to housing, or asking for work, they’re serving Pedro Sánchez,” the party’s leader, Santiago Abascal, said. “They’re Sánchez’s militias.”
Vox has also attempted to link the housing issue to migration. In a message posted on social media last month, the party falsely suggested that the 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked the mammoth protests would have had a home had she been an immigrant from north Africa.
In Belgium , where cost of living protests also escalated into street clashes in Brussels and Liège, the far-right Flemish nationalists of Vlaams Belang framed the rioting as a failure of integration and open borders, characterising it as “imported violence”.
Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni , has adopted another strategy – as head of a far-right government she has headed for four years, she cannot simply blame failures of the state. Instead, she has expanded her law-and-order agenda, and framed rioters as extremists.
“Demonstrating is a right, but setting our cities ablaze is not,” Meloni said after rioting in Milan and Bologna. “Hooligans have exploited the protests to sow chaos, attack those responsible for ensuring security, and hold entire cities hostage.”

Meloni has previously enacted sweeping security measures aimed at hindering public dissent, including jail terms for blocking roads, tough sentences for resisting police officers, and pre-detention for demonstrators thought likely to cause trouble.
This week she passed emergency decrees creating an offence of violent participation in ⁠a demonstration, imposing tougher penalties on ⁠rioters and organisers of violent groups, and penalising parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.
But she too has highlighted immigration as a factor, noting that “nearly half of those stopped or arrested” after the Milan riots were “of immigrant background, including individuals born abroad and second-generation children of immigrant families”.
Beyond Europe’s orthodox far-right parties, anti-immigration polemicists have gone further, interpreting the violence not as state and policy failures but as evidence of a looming civilisational war fuelled by multiculturalism and non-EU immigration.
Éric Zemmour, the founder of France’s Reconquête! (Reconquest) party, demanded an immigration halt and the deportation of “foreign delinquents”, declaring: “These are not riots, but the warning shots in an ethnic war. Either we establish absolute order or we yield.”
The far-right narrative has been reinforced by similar comments from the US, where both the president and vice-president have sought to turn the unrest in France in particular into a cautionary tale for voters before midterm elections.
Donald Trump described France as a once-great nation that had been “conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists”, adding on social media that immigration “has shattered that once great country”.
JD Vance echoed the same view, saying: “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion.” In doing so, they “ignored fundamental questions about assimilation and compatibility”, he said.

articles.title_orig: Turkey plans mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, ruling party official says
articles.title_zh: Turkey plans mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, ruling party official says
articles.content_orig:
The trilateral defence pact between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, also known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, has been submitted to the Turkish parliament for ratification.
The pact, signed on August 7, contains 16 articles, according to the document submitted to the Turkish parliament, seen by the Reuters news agency.
It aims to create a joint defence architecture in the region, in the case of an armed attack on any member, and lays out provisions in each article accordingly.
In Article 1 of the accord, for example, the signatories shall use “all necessary means” to eliminate threats to one another’s territorial integrity.
Once the first article is invoked, in case of an attack on any member state, the document lays out provisions for what follows next, as outlined in Article 2 of the draft seen by Reuters.
“In the event one of the parties is subjected to an armed attack or military aggression by another country or group of countries, the parties shall immediately provide assistance to the party under attack, utilising the full range ‌of mutual assistance measures available to them,” says Article 2.
This point is similar to Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, NATO’s founding document, which treats an armed attack on one member as an attack on all.
Article 2 goes on to say that each signatory – Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye – “will decide on the scope and nature of the support to be provided following an objective assessment of the assistance required”, adding that the three countries will cooperate within their available resources, including military capabilities and resources.
Earlier this month, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed to activate “deterrence measures” under the mutual defence pact and rapidly deploy forces to the Gulf kingdom to counter attacks by Yemen’s Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God).
Articles 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the draft agreement, submitted to the Turkish parliament, also lay out details on defence industry cooperation, intelligence sharing, logistical support and joint training and the fight against “all means of terrorism”, including at the operational level.
Other provisions talk about joint research, development and innovation projects in the field of advanced technology and ensuring military readiness.
There is also mention of setting up a defence committee, which will include foreign and defence ministers from all three signatory states.
And there is a mechanism for allowing other states to join the agreement, with aspirants needing the approval of all three founding members.
The agreement will last 10 years, after which any country can withdraw according to the draft submitted to the Turkish parliament.
Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar speaking on the submitted pact said the process of ratification is going to take “quite some time”, despite the ruling coalition needing a simple majority.
“The various political parties that are represented in the Turkish parliament are going to discuss the provisions in the pact, and we could witness heated debates because the opposition has its own objectives,” he said.
Serdar said even if the deal is ratified, it would not lead to a deployment of Turkish troops, a move which will require other legislative processes.
Turkiye’s parliamentary speaker will refer the agreement to ⁠the parliament’s foreign affairs commission. The commission could debate the ⁠agreement as early as Friday, according to a source who spoke to Reuters.
Once it is submitted to the commission, the contents and details of the agreement are expected to be made public.
“This strategic partnership developed between our countries aims to strengthen collective deterrence, enhance joint capabilities in the defence sector, and safeguard security and stability in our region,” Burhanettin Duran, the Turkish presidency’s communications director, said on X.
Duran added that the process marked an important milestone towards the “institutionalisation” of strategic cooperation between the three nations.
On Monday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke of the escalating violence between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis.
“As I often say, we are surrounded by a ring of fire. That is exactly the situation we face,” Erdogan said, while referring to the Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport.
In recent weeks, the Houthis have carried out missile and drone attacks against the kingdom, including oil facilities and Riyadh’s main airport, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the Yemeni government has launched air attacks on Houthi positions.

articles.title_zh: Mortgage rates drop for the first time in 2 months, but demand still falls further
articles.content_orig:
Mortgage demand took another leg lower, despite a brief respite from rising interest rates.
Total mortgage application volume fell 5.3% last week compared with the previous week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association's seasonally adjusted index.
The average contract interest rate for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages with conforming loan balances, $832,750 or less, dropped last week to 7.41% from 7.50%, with points falling to 0.75 from 0.83 including the origination fee for loans with a 20% down payment.
"Mortgage rates decreased for the first time in over two months," said Joel Kan, an MBA economist, in a release. "However, lower rates were not enough to boost application activity, as both purchase and refinance applications continued to decline."
Applications to refinance a home loan, which are most sensitive to weekly moves, fell just 2% week to week, a smaller drop than some previous weeks when rates were moving higher. Refinance demand was still 59% lower than the same week one year ago. With rates now over a full percentage point higher than they were a year ago, there is a very small pool of borrowers who can benefit from a refinance.
Applications for a mortgage to purchase a home declined a steeper 7% for the week and were 18% lower from the year before. Buyers are reacting less to the weekly move in rates but more to the overall higher level. A report from the National Association of Realtors on Tuesday showed a sharp drop in September pending home sales. These are measured by signed contracts, so it showed the real-time impact of rising rates during the month. Rates remained at that higher level in October.

For those buyers in the market, a continued high share are opting for adjustable-rate mortgages, or ARMs, which offer lower rates but are considered riskier because they will eventually reset to whatever the market rate is at the end of their term.
"The ARM share held steady at 10.5 percent, as ARM rates remained almost a full percentage point lower than the 30-year fixed rate, giving qualified borrowers a lower rate option to purchase a home," Kan added.
Mortgage rates haven't done much to start this week, according to a separate survey from Mortgage News Daily. Last week was a particularly volatile week for rates, due to multiple monthly inflation reports. This week the moves have seemed to follow oil prices.
"But we'd caution against placing too much emphasis on the oil price correlation," wrote Matthew Graham, chief operating officer at Mortgage News Daily. "It's been highly unreliable for more than a month."

Senior Technology Reporter

Apple may have been late to the foldable phone race, but the iPhone Duo sure hits its stride.
In the week I’ve spent with Apple’s long-awaited foldable phone , the iPhone Duo has shown just how intuitive one can be when hardware and software work in harmony. And while Apple may not have pioneered the passport-size phone , the Duo makes a compelling case for it being the most practical – and fun – foldable design. As such, the iPhone Duo has earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award.
Any first-generation product has its shortcomings. The iPhone Duo’s downsides aren’t dealbreakers, especially for how much it gets right. From the matte surface of the inner display that reduces glare to the durable yet sleek design to software that works seamlessly across both screens, the iPhone Duo’s finer details make the experience feel fluid and cohesive.
The price may be the biggest deterrent: The iPhone Duo costs $1,999 for 256GB, rising to $3,199 for 2TB of storage. While that starting point is high, it’s in line with most foldable phones like the $1,900 Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 , $2,100 Z Fold 8 Ultra and $1,899 Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold . The iPhone Duo’s steep price sure didn’t stop it from selling out almost instantly when preorders opened last week.
If anything, the Duo’s high cost and limited availability only reinforce that Apple’s foldable isn’t for everyone . But if you’re looking for something compact that unfurls into a tablet-like experience – and you want to stick with iOS – the iPhone Duo could be the right fit. Personally, I have no plans of switching back to a slab phone anytime soon.
It’s hard to be covert while using a product as eye-catching and highly anticipated as the iPhone Duo. The passport-size design makes me feel like a secret agent of sorts as I pry it open to jot down thoughts or fire off a text. (I suppose that’ll be even truer once Apple Pencil support drops later this month.) I drew plenty of curious looks while snapping photos around San Francisco and paying with Apple Pay, despite my best efforts to keep a low profile. If you get your hands on one, expect a few extra eyes on you, too.
It’s refreshing to use a phone that breaks from the bar-style design that’s dominated the market for years. Switching between two differently sized displays keeps the experience feeling dynamic. The 5.4-inch cover screen is great for quickly sending a message, checking a notification or snapping a photo. Meanwhile, the 7.6-inch inner display is optimized for watching horizontal videos in landscape mode and scrolling through vertical social content when the phone is rotated to portrait.
When closed, the iPhone Duo fits squarely in my palm and slips easily into just about any pocket — and I say that as a woman who owns clothes with tiny pockets. It unfolds with a slight springiness that makes it easy to open. Unfurled, the Duo resembles a smaller iPad Mini, but with a satisfying matte inner display that reduces glare and makes the center crease virtually invisible. (Tilt the phone with the screen locked and you’ll still see that line, but you won’t notice it while watching a show or scrolling through social media.) Apple says the inner display is also resistant to scratches and dents. I’ve been gentle with the phone, but both screens have held up without any scuffs so far.
One of the Duo’s most pleasing elements is that it opens fully flat – though when set on a tabletop, the camera bump prevents it from sitting completely flush against the surface. The phone doesn’t feel chunky even when closed, measuring 11.3mm thick when folded and 5.2mm when unfolded. That thinness helps the Duo mirror the feel of a tablet when open, making it the perfect size for watching videos or working on the go. In fact, I wrote the script for my accompanying review video entirely on the iPhone Duo, and I was thrilled not to have to lug a heavy laptop around.
The iPhone Duo thankfully has a Camera Control button , which I use extensively to quickly launch the camera. (You can also use it to access Apple’s Visual Intelligence , which gives information about objects and places around you.) The volume buttons are at the top of the Duo, which makes the most sense when the phone is rotated to portrait mode. It took some adjustment, but after a few days, I got used to the placement. When the phone is closed, it’s easy to reach up and access the buttons one-handed, thanks to the shorter screen. There’s no Action button , but I don’t miss it, since I hardly ever touch it on other iPhones. To turn on Silent Mode on the Duo, you’ll need to unlock the phone and go to the Control Center.
One of the iPhone Duo’s biggest drawbacks is the lack of Face ID . To unlock the phone, you’ll need to use Touch ID by placing your finger on the side button or typing in your password. This detracts from an otherwise premium experience; I’m so used to Face ID that its absence feels like a step backward. It’s not a deal-breaker, but unlocking the phone or using Apple Pay isn’t quite as fluid as it could be. Still, Touch ID’s high accuracy and speed help to make up for the slight inconvenience.
Despite the Duo’s compact 5.4-inch cover screen, it doesn’t feel cramped. I can comfortably do just about anything I would on a bar-style phone, just on a smaller scale. The keyboard is roomy, taking up around half the cover screen, so typing feels seamless and easy. I haven’t grappled with any more typos than usual. I tend to stick to the cover display for less-involved tasks such as checking an email, texting, ordering an Uber or snapping a photo.
When I’m doing something that requires more time or effort, I open the Duo to use its 7.6-inch inner display. That includes working in Google Docs, watching a YouTube video, streaming, scrolling through the Photos app or multitasking. Reading is a delight with the Duo’s matte display, which feels easier on the eyes, including while outdoors. The under-display FaceTime camera, which virtually disappears when not in use for a call or photo, also makes content look more immersive without a gaping black hole.
The Duo supports multitasking with up to two apps open at once, which split 50/50 on the inner screen when the phone is in landscape. Unfortunately, you can’t resize the apps to have one take up more space than another. By comparison, the Z Fold 8 can multitask with up to three resizable apps.
I like having video calls open on one side of the Duo’s screen and iMessage on the other, for instance, or playing a YouTube video while I shop online. It’s also handy being able to drag and drop images and files from one app to another and easily send them to a friend, as you can with other foldable phones. A neat Duo element is being able to “lock” two apps together, so if you swipe out, you can quickly pull the pair back up when scrolling through the App Switcher – no need to place them side-by-side again.
When the Duo is rotated to portrait, multitasking disappears and one app dominates the screen. That’s a bummer given how often I hold the phone vertically, but there is an exception: You can play a video in the upper portion of the screen using picture-in-picture while running another app below it. Instead of a 50/50 split, the video takes up a smaller portion of the screen at the top, with the second app dominating the rest. But if you fold the phone partway, it’ll split 50/50, so nothing is obstructed by the crease, which is a nice touch.
I have larger hands, so I can manage typing on the Duo’s inner screen in landscape, though it feels like a stretch. Typing is more comfortable on the inner display when it’s rotated to portrait, which also lends the screen the familiar feel of a sheet of paper or a physical do

articles.title_orig: Why are French protesters chanting ‘Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres’?
articles.title_zh: Why are French protesters chanting ‘Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres’?
articles.content_orig:
As violent protests roil France, bringing together students demanding better educational conditions and groups rejecting the high cost of living, one chant has become an improbable rallying cry: “Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres”.
The unofficial slogan does not mean much taken literally, but students have channelled a whole array of grievances that lie at the heart of the protest movement into this nonsensical expression. It is meant to mock racial stereotyping by the police.
Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets nationwide over the weekend, in the largest mobilisation since protests over education reforms and rising prices began last month. The protest movement has been triggered by grievances ranging from overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages to systemic inequality and lack of opportunity.
Police conduct has also come under scrutiny. France’s police inspectorate, the IGPN, has opened dozens of investigations into alleged police violence since protests began.
“Bismillah” is Arabic for “in the name of God”, an expression used by Muslims before beginning an activity. In French slang, it has lost some of its original meaning, becoming more akin to “let’s do it”.
“C’est les ténèbres” literally translates as “it’s the darkness”, which alludes to a situation that is bleak and hopeless.
The slogan therefore translates as “In the name of God, it’s the darkness”, which does not convey a clear message in and of itself.
Students say the phrase is a mockery of the police force, which tried to infiltrate social media chats used by protesters to coordinate.
The screenshot of a Snapchat conversation featuring the expression began circulating in early October. In it, a user named Mamadou requests to be added to a group, saying: “Hi, in the name of God, it’s the darkness. When’s the blockade, wallah, bro?”
The message also featured emojis with Algerian flags.
Students say the message was sent by undercover police officers attempting to infiltrate their chats by using an unconvincing mix of Arabic and slang. The claim has not been verified and French authorities have not issued any statement.
Youssef El Chazli, associate professor in Arab and Mediterranean sociology at Paris 8 University Vincennes – Saint-Denis, said the phrase “reinforces an image of out-of-touch policemen filled with stereotypes”.
“Such stereotypes appear to disproportionately aim at youths from Arab and African descent,” El Chazli told Al Jazeera. “This appears as one more example of how out-of-touch state agencies seem to be with the current movement.”
The slogan has appeared on cardboard placards as a mockery of racial stereotypes and as a symbol of how authorities are out of touch with the realities of young people.
The slogan has spread as far as Italy and Belgium, where similar protests over the high cost of living and poor education also took place over the weekend.
El Chazli said satirical memes and internet trends have become tools to express political grievances during protests, which have traditionally been “inventive and creative”. “With youth mobilisations, protest creativity will draw heavily on youths’ subcultures,” he said.
Discussions around Islamophobia have also taken a front seat in public debate. French authorities have been reluctant to comment publicly on a significant spike in Islamophobic acts in France. One report cited by the Reuters news agency last year showed a 72 percent increase in such incidents during the January-March quarter of 2025 compared with the same period in 2024.
The French far right quickly resorted to racist language to blame Muslim youths for the violence, while United States President Donald Trump also chimed in, claiming that this is about “Islam wanting to take over”.
“What used to be a nonsubject 20 years ago is now a debated point,” El Chazli said. “For younger generations, Arab and African influences have been steadily mainstreaming in youth subcultures, owing to sports and arts figures, as well as new radio shows or social media content.”

articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.content_orig:
You cannot fully block the two critical PHP flaws called PHP2Shell before today's fix, and the one setting being passed around as a workaround is not enough on its own, the security firm that suggested it now says.
PHP will release the fix at 14:00 UTC on October 21 for two flaws it rates 9.2 out of 10, and has given no workaround of its own. Until you can install it, what lowers your risk is taking exposed PHP off the internet or behind access controls, cutting what a compromised server can reach, and having the update ready to apply the moment it lands.
Cloudflare says it is seeing early attempts to exploit the flaws, and has pushed emergency rules for sites behind it that it calls a stopgap until you patch. No compromise has been confirmed, the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work, and neither flaw is in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws. PHP has not said which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, or whether any setting changes the risk; it says the full details and the fixed versions come with the release.
At the time of writing, that release was not yet out. So nobody outside the group that found the flaws can test whether a given defense works, which is why the advice below is about lowering risk, not promising safety.
The workaround spreading on social media and security blogs is one line in a PHP configuration file: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 . It turns off Session Upload Progress, a PHP feature that's enabled by default, which records how far a file upload has progressed so another request can check on it.
GMO Flatt Security, a Tokyo security firm, suggested setting it early on October 21, saying it could not be sure the change fully addresses the flaws but thought it would help with some probability.
Later the same day, the firm walked that back. In an update timestamped 14:00 Japan time (05:00 UTC), it said the setting alone is not a complete fix and that attacks getting around it are expected. It told administrators to prepare their update, watch for attack traffic before the release, and apply the fix as soon as it is out.
Two people from the PHP project said the same thing more bluntly. Replying to someone who suggested the upload-progress setting might patch the flaw, Gina Peter Banyard, a PHP core developer and documentation writer funded by the PHP Foundation, wrote : "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP. I sadly know too much." Joe Ferguson, the release manager for the coming PHP 8.6, put it shorter : "ini settings won't save you."
The setting cannot be relied on for two reasons. GMO Flatt expects a way around it but has not said what that is. And the whole idea that the flaw lives in Session Upload Progress is a guess: PHP has not confirmed it, the firm itself said it holds only so far as its own research matches PHP2Shell, and an independent code audit argues the specific bug others describe in that feature does not exist in released PHP. That audit is from an anonymous account and PHP's own code will settle it, but it is one more reason not to treat the setting as a shield.
Not everyone agrees. One vendor, Upwind, still lists the setting as an immediate mitigation , passing along another researcher's analysis rather than its own tests. watchTowr, which reproduced one of the flaws, says there is "no confirmed patch or workaround at this time."
No one is telling you to undo the change. The instruction is only not to count it as protection. PHP's own manual already advises turning the feature off where an application does not use upload progress bars, because the stored file names and field names "are not validated and may contain PHP code." If you turned it on by mistake somewhere that needs it, the only cost is that upload progress bars stop working.
Check that the change is actually in effect on the process that serves web traffic, not on the command line. The setting is INI_PERDIR, so it can be set in php.ini, .htaccess, or .user.ini.
A .user.ini file is read only by the CGI and FastCGI versions of PHP, not by the Apache module, and PHP re-reads it only every 300 seconds by default, so a change there can take five minutes to apply.
Under the Apache module, use .htaccess or the server config. Confirm the value on PHP-FPM or mod_php, whichever serves your site, not on php -i at the shell.
Get ready now. GMO Flatt's advice is to confirm your update steps and the checks you run afterward, rehearse any config change, and line up the people and approvals for a possible emergency restart. When the fix lands, update the runtime that serves web requests, which is PHP-FPM, mod_php, or CGI, not the application on top of it.
PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, 8.2 through 8.5. Which exact versions carry the fix and how far back the flaws extend will be announced with the release.
The Hacker News reported the branch support and the wider background in its earlier coverage of the disclosure.
Where an immediate update is not possible, CERT-EU advises organizations to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied." Banyard put the same point from inside the project: turning a server off for a day "might be the most sensible thing to do. But that is far from a reasonable thing to demand for most people." Short of shutting down, restrict reach: put the site behind a VPN, allowlisted clients, or authenticated access at the edge, and check that traffic cannot reach the origin directly around those controls.
Shrink what an attacker gets if the server is taken over. GMO Flatt's other steps are to reduce the data stored on the server, reduce its privileges, remove stored credentials, including cloud roles, and ensure logging is enabled and kept in a secure location so you can investigate later.
Branches older than 8.2, including 8.1, 7.x, and 5.x, are end-of-life and receive no PHP fixes. For those, upgrade, take the system offline, or isolate it; a Linux distribution or hosting provider may backport a fix on its own schedule.
A web application firewall is a stopgap here, not a fix, and Cloudflare says so itself. It has pushed emergency rules for the known exploit paths, free tier included, which its CTO calls "a STOPGAP only" ahead of patching. Such rules only see traffic that passes through Cloudflare, and they can miss new attack paths as they appear.
Updating WordPress, Laravel, or another application does not update the PHP runtime underneath it; that comes from your server package, host, or container image. On managed or shared hosting, ask your provider when a fixed PHP build will land and have them stand by.
Hosting providers build their packages only after PHP ships the fix: CloudLinux, for one, says its updated packages depend on the upstream release and will be posted when ready.
Exploitation is early and unconfirmed. Cloudflare reports emerging attempts; watchTowr says it reproduced one flaw but has not reported attacks; the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work; and neither flaw was in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws when it was last checked on October 21.
A researcher has posted a video said to demonstrate the exploit chain, and the audit above states that the circulating proof-of-concept code does not fire against released PHP. Treat all of this as a snapshot that can change by the hour.
When the fix ships, check the fixed version for your branch, which versions PHP lists as affected, whether PHP confirms or rejects any setting as a mitigation, and whether the session code changed, which also answers the dispute over where the flaw lives.
The fixed versions and the advisory will appear on php.net and through PHP's GitHub security advisories , where the project assigns its own identifiers. After updating, review your logs for anything that happened before you patched.

President Donald Trump on Tuesday vowed to treat potential rioters in the U.S. “very rough,” pointing to the unrest that has gripped France in recent days.
Trump made the remarks during a speech in Greenville, North Carolina, ahead of the midterm elections, after a heckler interrupted him as he campaigned for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley.
“They're crazy, these people. Look at that guy. He's a nutjob,” Trump said, referring to the protester in the crowd.
Trump warned that he would crack down on potential threats, saying he would not allow similar unrest to take hold in the U.S.
“That's what you witness over the last three or four days. You watch nutjobs like him in France ruining their country,” Trump said. “We're not going to put up with it by the way.”

Albanian police have clashed with anti-government protesters for an eighth consecutive day in the capital, Tirana , as demonstrators call for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, according to the Associated Press.
Similar to unrest sweeping across Europe, Albania’s protests have been fueled by discontent over rising fuel costs, the education system and a housing crisis, the AP said.
During the protests, demonstrators reportedly have hurled rocks, flares and firebombs at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.
Rama condemned the protests Tuesday, saying attempts to force political change through violence would never be allowed, according to the AP.
“A wave of stones, an attempt to overthrow the government and change those in power through the imposition of violence — something that will never be allowed to happen, in any form or for any reason,” Rama said Tuesday after a meeting with teachers and representatives of Tirana’s schools.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk on Tuesday condemned riots that have erupted across Europe over rising living costs, urging police to respond lawfully and calling for accountability for protesters who commit acts of violence and vandalism.
“I deplore the actions of those exploiting protests to commit acts of violence and vandalism against public and private property. They should be held individually accountable,” Turk said.
“I am concerned by reports of unnecessary and excessive use of force against protesters, including children. States must ensure that any law enforcement response remains lawful, necessary and proportionate. Allegations of unlawful use of force must be investigated promptly, effectively and independently, with accountability and effective remedies for victims.”
Türk called for “inclusive and safe dialogue” between governments and protesters to prioritize human rights concerns .

The additional military personnel will work alongside law enforcement through the end of year, while the government plans to expand judicial resources to ensure legal consequences for offenders, including some teenagers.
Under the measures, minors or their parents would also be required to pay for property they damage, the council said.

Authorities have imposed localized curfews as a result.

"Media report more curfews may follow for parts of Paris and in prefectures across the country, and that scattered protests could continue."

articles.title_zh: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.content_orig:
United States Special Envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian leaders on the Ukraine war following “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway.
Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday in the city in northwestern Russia, as the US pushes for an end to the war that began more than four and a half years ago with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Zelenskyy in recent weeks and has suggested that someone else should negotiate on Kyiv’s behalf. The remarks signalled a new low in their relationship, while Zelenskyy has accused the US of suspending crucial intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the talks between Witkoff and Zelenskyy as “positive”, adding that the US envoy would share the results with Putin. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also attended the talks with Zelenskyy, but did so virtually because of illness. Kushner is also expected to attend the meeting with Putin remotely.
“He’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side – and let’s see if we can make some progress,” Rubio said.
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland also attended the talks in Oslo. Representatives from the European Union and NATO were present. Following Tuesday’s talks, Zelenskyy said “very, very important” intelligence from the US had been restored.
Zelenskyy has also accused Washington of slowing down the internet service, Starshield, which is crucial for Ukraine’s battlefield operations. Starshield is the military-grade equivalent of Starlink and is also developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Rubio dismissed Zelenskyy’s accusations, saying Trump had “nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield”. Musk disputes this and says such decisions can only be made by the US military and president.
